The test image shows a tomato stem with white/powdery granular deposits along the stem surface, and somewhat distorted leaves. The stem hairs (trichomes) are visible and the white material appears to coat the stem between the hairs. Key features: stem-focused disease, white crusty/powdery deposits.

Top candidates: Powdery Mildew (white coating), Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato, Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato.

Now viewing one reference from each of 8 different classes:

Now analyzing all observations:

**Test image features:** White/grayish granular deposits uniformly distributed along a green tomato stem (aerial stem, not crown/base), stem still green and alive, leaves somewhat distorted/curled.

**Reference comparisons:**
- **Powdery Mildew** (CDDM_116, CDDM_78): White powdery patches on leaves — same type of white powdery material, just on different plant part. Powdery mildew CAN colonize stems.
- **Bacterial_Canker** (Bugwood_1): Brown leaf margin necrosis — not matching.
- **Alternaria_Stem_Cankers** (Bugwood_4): Dark necrotic canker at base — not matching.
- **Bacterial_Speck** (Bugwood_14): Small dark spots on leaves — not matching.
- **Sclerotinia** (Bugwood_12): Severe wilt/collapse — not matching.
- **Southern_Blight** (Bugwood_2): White mycelium but at crown/soil level, not aerial stem — partial similarity.
- **Bacterial_Wilt** (Bugwood_6): Whole-plant wilting — not matching.
- **Powdery_Mildew** (CDDM_78): White powdery surface coating on leaves — most visually consistent texture/color with the white deposits on the test stem.

The white granular powdery deposits on the aerial green stem match powdery mildew best — same white powdery texture seen on leaves in the Powdery Mildew references, just manifesting on the stem. No necrosis, no collapse, no dark lesions that would suggest other candidates.
